relevance_note: A three-generation family with HA20: 'identified a novel heterozygous c.2209delC mutation of TNFAIP3 in the members with HT', and 'P1–P7 were all diagnosed with HA20'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script assembled the JSON from my readings and checked spans, fields and labels. Tables 1 (thyroid function tests and anti-thyroid autoantibodies) and 2 (HLA typing) are present only as captions in the Markdown, so their values are not available; P3's and P4's antibody levels 'shown in Table 1' are therefore not recorded. Figures 1 (pedigree) and 2 were not available. Variant: the paper says the heterozygous c.2209delC mutation 'was present in all members tested' after analysing 'the present family (P1–P7)', and that 'P1–P7 were all diagnosed with HA20'; it never lists who was tested, so one variant row per P1–P7 was recorded with zygosity from that named-group sentence (this is the main uncertainty). Inheritance left 'not reported' for all: no individual parental carrier statement; relationships come only from the text and pedigree. Variant type not stated (no class given for c.2209delC); protein change not printed. Pathogenicity combines 'novel' (Results/Abstract) with 'previously reported as a pathogenic mutation (2)'; functional evidence is only a citation to ref 2. Ages for P1, P6, P7 ('currently 6-, 2-, and 1-yr-old, respectively') assigned in order. HT ages (P2 28 yr, P3 27 yr) are ages at HT diagnosis, recorded on the HT feature rows, not as age at HA20 diagnosis. Hedged findings were not recorded as observed: P2 'suggestive of inflammatory bowel disease' and 'Colonoscopy revealed possible Crohn’s disease' (symptoms resolved spontaneously); P7 perineal fistula is recorded with the authors' 'possibly associated with inflammatory bowel disease' wording, but checklist GI inflammation left not reported. Stomatitis (P3, P4) was not mapped to the 'oral ulcers' checklist item because ulcers are not stated. P2's chronic mild hepatitis is not called autoimmune, so autoimmune hepatitis is not reported. P4's Hodgkin lymphoma and craniopharyngioma were not mapped to lymphoproliferation or CNS involvement. P1, P6, P7: 'normal thyroid functions and no anti-thyroid autoantibodies, but are too young for this to be apparent' recorded as excluded 'abnormal thyroid function' and 'anti-thyroid autoantibodies' (D-27); autoimmune thyroiditis checklist left not reported given the authors' hedge, and the narrower anti-thyroid antibody absence does not exclude 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)'. Four previously published HA20 patients from the Discussion have individual-level features and were included per v4: ref (2) patient (psoriatic arthritis, spondylitis, aortic insufficiency; HLA-B27 not recorded as a variant), ref (2) patient 2 (GD with TRAb/TPOAb/TgAb), ref (15) patient (HT), ref (4) patient (Takagi et al.; ALPS-like, increased DNT). No variant rows for them (no variant printed or tied explicitly). The two ref (2) patients could overlap with members of this family, which was also described in ref 2; the paper does not say. Ethnicity of the family left not reported: the paper only says the family was part of Kadowaki et al.'s study of 'nine independent Japanese families'. Sex of P1 and P6 not stated. No contradictions found.
